It makes sense to feel discouraged when therapy didn't help before—that's a real and valid frustration. But one experience four years ago doesn't have to define what's possible now. Therapy isn't one-size-fits-all: the approach, the therapist, and even where you are in your own life can make a big difference. For PTSD specifically, there are evidence-based treatments like EMDR, prolonged exposure, or cognitive processing therapy that some people find helpful even after other approaches didn't work.

The fact that you're saying "I need help" is important—it shows you haven't given up on yourself. You might consider looking for someone who specializes in trauma, and it's okay to ask a potential provider directly how their approach differs from what you tried before.

If you're ever feeling unsafe or in crisis, please reach out to a crisis line (you can call or text 988 in the US) or emergency services. What kind of help feels most needed for you right now?
